source_title: New Single-Player FPS Games Confirmed Coming Soon, Ranked - GameRant
source_excerpt:
Call of Duty: Black Ops 7 is out, but that doesn't mean you don't have any new FPS games to look forward to. Admittedly, November 2026 isn't absolutely stuffed with shooters, and we must look beyond the absolute mainstream to find some titles that could end up being fantastic. While not massive, the lineup offers quite a bit of variety, covering sci-fi horror, co-op, open-world, and two roguelites. A healthy range of FPS goodness.
As none of these are necessarily year-defining releases, these games might very well slip through the cracks for most folks, which would be a shame since they could prove to be among 2026's best shooters. Therefore, I'm going to give a rundown of November 2026's upcoming FPS games, just to provide an overview.
This is by no means a comprehensive lineup, and I would recommend checking Steam's upcoming releases section for more games.
I'm also going to omit upcoming Early Access releases, but ALTEREDBLOOD+ looks very promising.
1 Void/Breaker Leaves Early Access On November 4
An FPS Game All About Total Environmental Destruction
This one almost feels like a cheat, as Void/Breaker has been out for a while, with the game entering Steam Early Access in August 2025. After just over a year, Stubby Games feels ready to release the full 1.0 version, a culmination of a reliable and consistent roadmap . For those who have already bought in, they can look forward to the final zone and the story's conclusion, a new boss, new weapons, an endgame hub, and more.

For those who have never heard of Void/Breaker , you should definitely have this on your radar, as long as you are relatively fine with a roguelite movement shooter. The game has plenty of things going for it, but its main selling point is its voxel destruction , as players can blast through walls and reshape the environment, one shell at a time. Weapon crafting and modding make up the heart of the progression system, and you will quickly be drowning in ways to tweak your gun.
The PS1 might not exactly be synonymous with first-person shooters, but that era just had a certain vibe that is entirely its own, which might explain why we still get so many throwbacks that somewhat replicate this aesthetic. Derelikt specifically calls out System Shock 2 , Doom 3 , and Alien Resurrection (nice!) as inspiration for its mood and structure, along with dropping a Silent Hill mention for extra cred. Yeah, November has a sci-fi horror retro shooter.
Players find themselves trapped in an outpost on an asteroid that seems to have fallen on hard times, leaving only a few humans to tell the tale (and they don't really seem to be on the same page). Explore, talk to NPCs, shoot things that could give you nightmares, and preserve your bullets and health packs as you will need them.
Even though I am currently primarily into fast-paced movement shooters , I can easily admit that Derelikt looks absolutely brilliant, and the demo should give you a good idea of what to expect.
3 Deadboot Blasts Onto Steam On November 5
An FPS Game That Arms You With Guns, Bats, And A Foot
Image by GameRant; Source:ULTRAKAOS Games
Image by GameRant; Source:ULTRAKAOS Games
Image by GameRant; Source:ULTRAKAOS Games
Deadboot is a simple roguelite FPS game , and I mean that as a compliment. The goal is to climb your way up a tower, wiping out every living thing along the way. After every floor, you pick one upgrade and might even unlock a new gun; then, it is immediately back to killing. Yeah, this might not sound too exciting on paper, but Deadboot just feels good to play, at least going by the demo.
Although gunplay is certainly the focus, it isn't your only course of action, as you are often simultaneously armed with a melee weapon that can do some serious close-range damage. More importantly, you have your boot, and a well-placed kick can send an enemy flying into a meat grinder and a quick death. In some ways, Deadboot kind of reminds me of Mullet Madjack , albeit with more open, traditional levels.
OK, let's end things with a bit of a weird one, and I don't mean that in a negative way. Havker-Man X classifies itself as an open-world FPS immersive sim with a somewhat psychedelic aesthetic. Just looking at the screenshots, you might get flashbacks to Cruelty Squad , which very much seems to have inspired this upcoming shooter. That said, Havker-Man X 's gunplay leans into run-and-gun arcade territory a bit more than that indie darling.
Honestly, this is one of those releases that I would recommend trying the demo to decide whether this is for you or not. From what I've played, Havker-Man X should be a worthwhile addition to the immersive sim space, especially since we really don't get all that many of these projects nowadays.
